edges.description: The gain-of-function variant increases the Slack (KNa) potassium current.
The enhanced potassium current alters neuronal firing patterns, including in inhibitory interneurons.

edges.description: Disrupted firing and impaired inhibition produce multifocal cortical hyperexcitability.
edges.source: Disrupted Neuronal Firing and Interneuron Dysfunction

edges.description: Independent multifocal hyperexcitability generates seizures that migrate across cortical regions.
The relentless seizure burden and underlying channel dysfunction drive severe developmental impairment.
The generated seizure pattern is observed clinically as migrating focal seizures, the defining feature of the syndrome.
Because the migrating seizures are near-continuous, they frequently evolve into refractory status epilepticus.
Ictal spread to autonomic networks produces the common perioral cyanosis, flushing, and apnea accompanying the seizures.
The relentless epileptic activity superimposed on the channel defect is the epileptic encephalopathy itself.
The encephalopathy is expressed clinically as profound global developmental delay.
Milestone plateau or regression accompanies seizure onset as the encephalopathy establishes itself.
Head growth falls off postnatally, typically by age 12 months; the intermediates linking the encephalopathy to arrested brain growth are not established.
Axial hypotonia is part of the neurologic picture accompanying the encephalopathy, through intermediates that have not been resolved.

nodes.description: Microcephaly develops postnatally, typically by age 12 months.

nodes.description: The enhanced Slack current alters the firing of cortical neurons; a leading interpretation is that its effect on inhibitory interneurons paradoxically disinhibits the network. This node captures the single concept of the altered firing/inhibition.

nodes.description: The relentless epileptic activity contributes to a severe encephalopathy.

The gain-of-function variant markedly increases the amplitude of the sodium-activated potassium (KNa) current carried by the Slack channel. This node captures the single concept of the enhanced potassium conductance and conforms to the shared epilepsy final common pathway.

in total identifying mutations in 6 out of 12 unrelated affected individuals

nodes.description: A gain-of-function variant in KCNT1, which encodes the sodium-activated potassium channel Slack (KNa1.1), is the most common cause of EIMFS. This node captures the single concept of the initiating channel lesion.

evidence.snippet: We performed exome sequencing in three probands with MMPSI and identified de novo gain-of-function mutations affecting the C-terminal domain of the KCNT1 potassium channel

nodes.description: Focal seizures arise independently in both hemispheres and migrate from one cortical region to another, often nearly continuously and with status epilepticus. This node captures the single concept of the characteristic seizure pattern and conforms to the shared epilepsy final common pathway.
Focal seizures that arise independently in both hemispheres and migrate across cortical regions are the defining feature.

Multiple cortical regions in both hemispheres become independently hyperexcitable and epileptogenic. This node captures the single concept of multifocal network hyperexcitability and conforms to the shared epilepsy final common pathway.

Quinidine, a partial blocker of the Slack (KCNT1) channel, has been used as a precision therapy that targets the gain-of-function mechanism. In a systematic review of KCNT1-related epilepsy it benefited a subset of EIMFS patients (about 45%), with variable responses and required cardiac QT monitoring.
Seizures are frequently prolonged, near-continuous, and evolve into status epilepticus.
Profound global developmental delay with arrest or regression of milestones is characteristic.

Profound global developmental impairment accompanies and is aggravated by the relentless seizures, with acquired microcephaly and movement abnormalities common. This node captures the single concept of the encephalopathic outcome.
